aspects.says: A call whose input never changes can be computed once, so a benchmark must vary its inputs as production does.
basis: section:A Benchmark Measures Nothing When the JIT Can Drop the Work or Fold Its Input

aspects.says: With an interface, the same load changed nothing; the first call with the new class made the code not entrant.
basis: section:Compiled Code Rests on Assumptions, and a Class Loaded Later Can Make It Not Entrant

aspects.says: Interpreted, the same loop ran 38 to 56 times slower than C2's code, so each method is slow until it crosses its threshold.
basis: section:Until the Compiled Code Is Installed, the Same Loop Runs Tens of Times Slower
aspects.reason: a speed ratio depends on the machine and the JIT's timing, which no deterministic test can check; the quiz checks what the timings mean

aspects.says: Code C2 compiled on the assumption that a class's method has one implementation is made not entrant when an overriding class loads, even if it is never called, and runs slower until C2 compiles it again.
basis: section:Compiled Code Rests on Assumptions, and a Class Loaded Later Can Make It Not Entrant

aspects.says: An OSR compile that never saw its loop exit is thrown away when the loop ends, so a second call can be slower than the first.
basis: section:Until the Compiled Code Is Installed, the Same Loop Runs Tens of Times Slower

aspects.says: A % line is an on-stack replacement compile of a loop, which a running call jumps into; it is not the code a new call enters.
basis: section:A Method Starts in the Interpreter and Is Compiled in Tiers Once Its Counters Say It Is Hot

aspects.says: A lower tier's code made not entrant after a newer compile of the same method was installed is a replacement: calls go to the newer code.
basis: section:A Method Starts in the Interpreter and Is Compiled in Tiers Once Its Counters Say It Is Hot

aspects.says: A method runs in the interpreter until its call and loop counters cross a threshold, then is compiled by C1 at tier 3 with profiling and by C2 at tier 4 from that profile; a trivial getter goes to tier 1.
basis: section:A Method Starts in the Interpreter and Is Compiled in Tiers Once Its Counters Say It Is Hot

aspects.says: A benchmark that times its first rounds measures the compiler's work, so the timing starts after the warm-up.
basis: section:Until the Compiled Code Is Installed, the Same Loop Runs Tens of Times Slower
section:A Benchmark Measures Nothing When the JIT Can Drop the Work or Fold Its Input

aspects.says: A loop whose results nobody uses can be deleted by the JIT, so it measures nothing; every result must reach something the JIT can't see through.
basis: section:A Benchmark Measures Nothing When the JIT Can Drop the Work or Fold Its Input
